# How DQC works

DQC is a set of Airflow operators to help identify and alert Data Quality Issues. You can plug it in any of your Airflow DAGs. It will execute SQL query and check if the data is expected with your own configuration. It supports notification on email/Slack/PagerDuty. 

In general you have two options to use DQC: 

* Configure entirely by you self using **DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator**  
* Use existing operators which are already wrapped by us 

### 1\. Import module 

On legacy Airflow (Clroot): 

| from data\_sci.airflow\_operators.tahoe.functional\_operator import DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator, DQValueCheckOperator |
| :---- |

On Airflow 2.0 (data-pipelines)

| from src.contrib.data\_sci.data\_quality\_operator import DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator, DQValueCheckOperator |
| :---- |

### 2\. Choose the operator 

You can have a glance at the section “Available Operators” below. Each operator is designed to solve specific problems. Of course you can alway use **DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator** to make the most flexible check. You can refer to [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fKSzv8Bzzhoht7PX9B5CvHABdzpvdmumC_-PaFLzN8o/edit) to find the usage of each operator for certain data quality issues. 

### 3\. Provide SQL and threshold 

* For **DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator,**  you need to provide SQL query and a ***validate\_func*** which takes the query result (list\<dict\>) as input and returns pass\_flag(boolean; if the test passes/fails) and log\_in\_detail(string; this message will be in the notification/leave it as empty string if you don’t want to add any message). You need to implement the rules inside your validate\_func.   
* For **DQValueCheckOperator**, you need to configure some input variables to let the operator ensemble SQL query and validate\_func. You can take the demo below as an example.  The **value**   
  inside column\_map is a Python list representing the expected value range; for example, for the aggregated value count(tracking\_id), we expect its value to be in \[1, ∞). Anything outside such range will yield the alert. 

---

  DQValueCheckOperator(  
     task\_id\='dqc\_value\_check',  
     dag\=dag,  
     db\='wishpost',  
     table\='wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle',  
     column\_map\={'tracking\_id\_cnt': {'expression': 'count(tracking\_id)',  
                                     'value': \[1, float('inf')\]},  
                 'shipping\_country\_cnt': {'expression': 'count(distinct shipping\_country)',  
                                          'value': \[1, 5\]}

                 },

     dimension\=\['dt'\],

     partition\_condition\="""dt \= '{{ds}}'""",

     extra\_condition\='order\_created\_time \> 1648778400',

     dependencies\=\[dqc\_hist\_task\]

  )

---

We have in-class documentation for each operator in case you want to know how to use them.   
More details can also be found in [the design doc](https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1vnauoR6B-ThlQogPkqyHRtRq3H97MjHCVbCByjRmbQU/edit)   
Contact us if you have any questions :) [Jialiang Cui](mailto:jcui@contextlogic.com)[Raymond Xu](mailto:raxu@contextlogic.com)[Evelyn Bai](mailto:ebai@contextlogic.com)

# Available Operators

| No. | Operator Name(Inherits From) | Usage Example | Details |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | **DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator (NaivePythonOperator)** | dqc\_free\_form \= DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator(   task\_id\='dqc\_free\_sql\_check',   dag\=dag,   sql\_query\="""           select is\_registered, count(1) as cnt           from wishpost.dim\_order\_channel\_cn\_mongo           where is\_registered is not null           group by 1    """,   validate\_func\=demo\_validate\_func,   slack\_alert\=True,   slack\_channel\='\#dqc-slack-alert-test',   slack\_recipients=\[‘jcui’, ‘raxu’, ‘ebai’\] ,  failed\_pipeline\=False )  | \- ***sql\_query*** is provided by user \- ***validate\_func*** takes the result of sql\_query as input, returns pass\_flag, log\_in\_detail \- when pass\_flag return False,    alert messages will be sent. Default alert method is email. Recipients use dag owner as default, and can also be overridden as a list of stringE.g. \[‘name1’, ‘name2’, ‘name3’\] \- Alert messages can also be sent via slack. Simply set ***slack\_alert*** to True, specify ***slack\_channel***, and ***slack\_recipients***(dag owner as default)**There are** **some prerequisites for receiving Slack notifications, see below for details**  \- ***failed\_pipeline*** indicates whether the rest of the tasks will proceed when the DQC task fails. If set to ***True,*** the rest tasks will not proceed, and the pipeline will be set to be failed.   |
| 2 | **DQValueCheckOperator (DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator)** | dqc\_value\_task \= DQValueCheckOperator(    task\_id\='dqc\_value\_check',    dag\=dag,    db\='wishpost',    table\='wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle',    column\_map\={'tracking\_id\_cnt': {'expression': 'count(tracking\_id)',                                    'value': \[1, float('inf')\]},                'shipping\_country\_cnt': {'expression': 'count(distinct shipping\_country)',                                         'value': \[1, 5\]}                },    dimension\=\['dt'\],    partition\_condition\="""dt \= '{{ds}}'""",    extra\_condition\='order\_created\_time \> 1648778400',    dependencies\=\[dqc\_hist\_task\] )  | \- sql\_query is generated based on ***column\_map, dimension***, and any ***conditions*** provided in the Operator Params. The  example on the left will generate the sql as this: ‘      select order\_channel, dt, count(distinct shipping\_country) as shipping\_country\_cnt, count(tracking\_id) as tracking\_id\_cnt            from wishpost.wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle            where 1 \= 1            and dt \= '2022-07-10'            and order\_created\_time \> 1648778400            group by order\_channel, dt ’\-  |
| 3 | **DQDuplicateCheckOperator (DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator)**  | dqc\_duplicate\_task \= DQDuplicateCheckOperator(    task\_id\='dqc\_duplicate\_check',    dag\=dag,    db\='wishpost',    table\='wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle',    column\='carrier\_pickup\_state',    partition\_condition\="""dt \= '{{ds}}'""",    extra\_condition\='order\_created\_time \> 1648778400', ) | \-sql\_query is generated based on the column and any ***conditions*** provided in the Operator Params. Check if there’s duplicate key values in a column. The example on the left will generate the sql as this: select cnt\_duplicate\_value, count(1) as cnt\_record             from             (                 select carrier\_pickup\_state, count(1) as cnt\_duplicate\_value                 from wishpost.wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle                 where 1 \= 1                 and dt \= '2022-06-27'                 and order\_created\_time \> 1648778400                 group by 1             ) t             group by 1 |
| 4 | **DQHistoricalValueCheckOperator (DQValueCheckOperator)**  | dqc\_hist\_task \= DQHistoricalValueCheckOperator(    task\_id\='dqc\_historical\_check',    dag\=dag,    db\='core\_data',    table\='fct\_transaction\_variations',    column\_map\={'gmv': {'expression': 'sum(gmv\_variation)',                        'value': \[-0.03, 0.03\]},                'txns': {'expression': 'count(distinct transaction\_id)',                         'value': \[\]},                'users': {'expression': 'count(distinct user\_id)',                          'value': \[\]},                'gmv\_per\_user': {'expression': 'sum(gmv\_variation)\*1.0/count(distinct user\_id)',                                 'value': \[\]},             },    dimension\=\['dt'\],    partition\_condition\="""dt \>= '{{macros.ds\_add(ds, \-7)}}' """,    dependencies\=\[dqc\_free\_form\],    fail\_pipeline\=False )  | \- sql\_query is generated based on ***column\_map***, ***dimension***, and any ***conditions*** provided in the Operator Params.   The example on the left will generate the sql as this: select dt,  count(distinct transaction\_id) as txns, sum(gmv\_variation)\*1.0/count(distinct user\_id) as gmv\_per\_user, sum(gmv\_variation) as gmv, count(distinct user\_id) as users              from                           core\_data.fct\_transaction\_variations         where 1 \= 1  and dt \>= '2022-06-07'  group by d![][image1]t |
| 5 | **DQRegexMatchOperator (DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator)** | dqc\_regex\_check \= DQRegexMatchOperator(    task\_id\='dqc\_regex\_check',    dag\=dag,    db\='wishpost',    table\='wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle',    column\='tracking\_id',    regex\='(^W.\*FPL$)|^UD',    partition\_condition\="""dt \= '{{ds}}'""",    extra\_condition\='order\_created\_time \> 1648778400' ) | \-sql query is generated based on user-defined target ***column***, target ***regex expression***, together with any ***conditions*** provided in the Operator Params. \-check if all values in the target column match with the regex expression. The example on the left will generate the sql as this:  select count(tracking\_id) as cnt         from wishpost.wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle         where 1=1         and not regexp\_like(tracking\_id, '(^W.\*FPL$)|^UD')         and dt \= '2022-06-22'         and order\_created\_time \> 1648778400 The alert email be like: ![][image2] |
| 6 | **DQValueInSetCheckOperator (DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator)** | dqc\_value\_task5 \= DQValueInSetCheckOperator(    task\_id \= 'dqc\_value\_equality\_check\_2',    dag\=dag,    db\='wishpost',    table\='wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle',    column\_map\={        'registered': {            'expression': 'registered',            'value': \['true'\]        },        'cancel\_src': {            'expression': 'cancel\_source',            'value': \[1\]        }    },    partition\_condition\="""dt \= '{{ds}}'""",    extra\_condition\='order\_created\_time \> 1648778400', ) | \-User needs to specify a ***column\_map*** where the key is the alias of selected columns or aggregation expressions, and other ***conditions*** used to generate the sql.  \-This operator solves data issues under condition of: Check if all values in target column(s) are in a predefined set Check if aggregation of target column(s) is in a predefined set It can also solve value equality data issues by setting the predefined set to a specific number. The example on the left will generate a sql like this: select distinct registered, cancel\_src from             (select  registered as registered, cancel\_source as cancel\_src             from wishpost.wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle             where 1 \= 1             and dt \= '2022-06-22'             and order\_created\_time \> 1648778400                          ) as t order by 1 \-In the alert email, the alert log is meaningful, but data summary will be the cartesian product of elements in two columns. ![][image3]  |
| 7 | **DQDualValueCheckOperator (DQFreeFormSQLCheckOperator)** | dqc\_dual\_value\_task \= DQDualValueCheckOperator(    task\_id\='dqc\_value\_check',    dag\=dag,    db\='wishpost',    table\='wishpost\_order\_clean\_full\_cycle',    column\_map\={'tracking\_id\_cnt': {'expression': 'count(tracking\_id)',    'value': \[1, 10000 \],   'hard\_check\_value': \[0, float('inf')\],          },                'shipping\_country\_cnt': {'expression': 'count(distinct       shipping\_country)', 'value': \[1, 5\]}                },    dimension\=\['dt'\],    partition\_condition\="""dt \= '{{ds}}'""",    extra\_condition\='order\_created\_time \> 1648778400',    dependencies\=\[dqc\_hist\_task\] )  | \- allow dual value criteria check on columns \- Operator checks the ***‘hard\_check\_value’*** first, if pass\_dqc fails, the task will terminate and pipeline will be set to fail. \- If ***‘hard\_value\_check’*** passed and ***‘value’*** doesn’t, alert messages will still be sent via email or slack, but the pipeline will continue.  \- ![][image4] ![][image5]  |
| 8 | **DQDualHistoricalValueCheckOperator (DQValueCheckOperator)** | dqc\_hist\_task \= DQDualHistoricalValueCheckOperator(    task\_id\='dqc\_dual\_historical\_check',    dag\=dag,    db\='core\_data',    table\='fct\_transaction\_variations',    column\_map\={'gmv': {'expression': 'sum(gmv\_variation)',                        'value': \[-0.03, 0.03\],                        ‘hard\_check\_value’: \[-1, 1\]                        },                'txns': {'expression': 'count(distinct transaction\_id)',                         'value': \[\]},                'users': {'expression': 'count(distinct user\_id)',                          'value': \[\]},                'gmv\_per\_user': {'expression': 'sum(gmv\_variation)\*1.0/count(distinct user\_id)',                                 'value': \[\]},             },    dimension\=\['dt'\],    partition\_condition\="""dt \>= '{{macros.ds\_add(ds, \-7)}}' """,    dependencies\=\[dqc\_free\_form\],    fail\_pipeline\=False )  | \- allow dual historical value criteria check on columns \- if ***‘hard\_check\_value’*** is provided, Operator checks it first and fail the task & pipeline if value out of range    ![][image6] |

# Set up Slack Notification

**Steps for integrating Default SlackBot App** \[DataQualityCheck-Test\]

* Choose a channel that you want to receive your alert message  
* Click View All Members  
              ![][image7]

  Under ‘*Integration*’’ , click ‘Add apps’  
  ![][image8]  
    
  Search for app named *‘DataQualityCheck-Test’ , click add*   
  *![][image9]*  
* Now you are good to go. Specify the correct slack channel name in your DQC Operators and you will receive your alert messages when needed

*![][image10]*

**Steps for Creating your own SlackBot App**

* **Go to [https://api.slack.com/apps?new\_app=1](https://api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1)**  
* **Click *‘Create New App’***   
  **![][image11]**

* **Specify app name and workspace**   
  **![][image12]**  
* **Request Installation of your app (takes some time to get approved)**  
  **![][image13]**  
* **Add all necessary features and permissions of your app**  
  **![][image14]**

* **After a request is approved, an Oauth Token will be generated. Use it as the token for authenticating your app.(e.g. Slack\_token parameter of DQC Operators)**  
  **![][image15]**  
* **When successfully installed, you can search your app under your workspace. ![][image16]**


# 

# Integrate PagerDuty 

It is easy to trigger PagerDuty alert, all you need to do is set up the following parameters:

- pagerduty\_alert (please set this to True)  
- pagerduty\_severity (like ‘Info’ or ‘Warning’ or etc)  
- pagerduty\_notify (the group you are in such as ‘cde-data’)

Attention\! Only DQC on Airflow 2.0 supports PagerDuty alert\!
